prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Beneath these fruit-tree boughs that shed Their snow-white blossoms on my head, With brightest sunshine round me spread Of spring's unclouded weather, In this sequestered nook how sweet To sit upon my orchard-seat! And birds and flowers once more to greet, My last year's friends together. One have I marked, the happiest guest In all this covert of the blest: Hail to Thee, far above the rest In joy of voice and pinion! Thou, Linnet! in thy green array, Presiding Spirit here to-day, Dost lead the revels of the May; And this is thy dominion. While birds, and butterflies, and flowers, Make all one band of paramours, Thou, ranging up and down the bowers, Art sole in thy employment: A Life, a Presence like the Air, Scattering thy gladness without care, Too blest with any one to pair; Thyself thy own enjoyment. Amid yon tuft of hazel trees, That twinkle to the gusty breeze, Behold him perched in ecstasies, Yet seeming still to hover; There! where the flutter of his wings Upon his back and body flings Shadows and sunny glimmerings, That cover him all over. My dazzled sight he oft deceives, A brother of the dancing leaves; Then flits, and from the cottage-eaves Pours forth his song in gushes; As if by that exulting strain He mocked and treated with disdain The voiceless Form he chose to feign, While fluttering in the bushes.

### Option 1: Sophisticated Narrative Prose (Best for professional essays, presentations, or descriptive writing)

> Beneath a canopy of fruit-tree branches shedding snow-white blossoms upon me, surrounded by the radiant sunshine of an unclouded spring day, it is a profound delight to sit in this secluded orchard nook. Here, I am reunited with the birds and flowers—my cherished companions from the previous year. 
> 
> Among all the inhabitants of this blessed sanctuary, one guest stands out as the most joyful of all. Preeminent in the exuberance of its voice and flight, the Linnet—adorned in vibrant green plumage—serves as the presiding spirit of the day, leading the springtime festivities over its rightful domain. 
> 
> While the surrounding birds, butterflies, and blossoms unite in pairs of mutual devotion, the Linnet roams freely through the bowers, solitary in its pursuits. Existing as a presence as ambient and effortless as the air, it radiates unreserved happiness—too self-sufficient in its joy to require a mate, finding complete contentment within itself.
> 
> Within a nearby cluster of hazel trees fluttering in the gusty breeze, the bird perches in ecstasy, appearing almost to hover in place. There, the rapid motion of its wings casts a shimmering interplay of light and shadow across its back and body. It frequently tricks my dazzled eyes, blending so seamlessly into the scenery as to seem a kin to the dancing leaves. Then, flitting upward to the cottage eaves, it pours forth an exuberant torrent of song—as though its triumphant melody were intended to mock the silent, motionless disguise it had just assumed while hiding in the bushes.

outputs.L2:
Underneath the branches of fruit trees that scatter white petals onto my head, I sit in the brilliant, clear sunlight of a lovely spring day. Resting on a bench in this secluded corner of the orchard brings me immense pleasure as I welcome back the local plants and birds—companions I came to know during the previous year.

Among all the creatures in this sheltered sanctuary, I have singled out one visitor who seems happier than all the rest. I offer special praise to this bird, whose vibrant song and swift wings make it superior to every other animal here. It is a green-feathered linnet, acting as the leader of today’s spring festivities in a domain over which it rules completely.

While the surrounding butterflies, birds, and blossoms mingle together like a group of devoted lovers, the linnet flies up and down through the branches, entirely focused on its own unique activity. It moves like a constant force of nature, effortlessly spreading joy all around. It is so utterly content within itself that it has no need for a partner, deriving full satisfaction purely from its own existence.

Nearby, in a cluster of hazel trees that shimmer whenever a sharp gust of wind blows, the bird perches in pure bliss, looking as though it is still hovering in mid-air. As its wings flutter, they cast a shifting pattern of bright light and dark shadows that completely cover its body and back.

Its rapid movements frequently trick my overwhelmed vision, making the bird look just like one of the rustling leaves on the trees. Moments later, it flies away to the roof edges of a small house and pours out a sudden stream of passionate music. Through this triumphant melody, it seems to mock and look down upon the quiet, motionless shape it had pretended to be while hiding in the bushes just moments before.
outputs.L3:
On a radiant spring day, the speaker retreats into the tranquil sanctuary of a secluded orchard, taking immense delight in the seasonal renewal of the natural world. Surrounded by blooming flowers and active woodland creatures, the speaker experiences a warm, joyful reunion with the vibrant flora and fauna that have returned to mark the end of winter's slumber.

Yet, amid this rich chorus of life, one creature stands out above all others. The speaker singles out the Green Linnet as the supreme herald of the season. More than just a songbird, the Linnet is crowned as the most joyous resident of the orchard—the very presiding spirit of spring, embodying the unbridled exuberance of nature’s rebirth.

What makes the Linnet particularly fascinating is its solitary and self-contained nature. While other creatures spend the season busily seeking companions or building nests, the Linnet flits about independently. It has no need for a mate to complete its happiness; rather, it finds absolute satisfaction in its own carefree existence, delighting simply in the act of being alive.

Visually, the bird seems to merge with its surroundings. Perched ecstatically among the slender boughs of hazel trees, the Linnet moves with such grace that it becomes almost indistinguishable from the swaying foliage. As breeze and canopy move together, dappled sunlight and soft shadows flicker across the bird’s green wings, painting a mesmerizing picture of harmony between the creature and its woodland home. 

Finally, the Linnet engages in a playful game with anyone watching. It quietly conceals itself within the dense foliage, tricking the observer into thinking it has vanished, only to suddenly dart out and land upon the nearby cottage eaves. There, in full view, the bird opens its throat to pour out an exultant, triumphant song—filling the orchard with the definitive melody of a bright spring day.
outputs.L4:
The busyness of the world fades away as I find retreat within the sequestered sanctuary of a sunlit orchard. It is the height of spring, a time when the earth seems to hold its breath in quiet anticipation of growth. Golden light filters through a dense canopy of young foliage, scattering dappled shadows across the soft, blossom-strewn grass below. Here, far from human distraction, the air is thick with the sweet, fresh scent of flower buds and damp earth. I settle into the silence, surrendering my mind to the gentle rhythms of the surroundings, content to simply sit, observe, and absorb the peaceful stillness of the day.

As my senses adjust to the quiet, my gaze is drawn upward into the swaying boughs of an old apple tree. A subtle shift in the greenery catches my eye—a swift, fleeting motion that vanishes almost as soon as it appears. I focus my attention intently on the foliage, searching for the source of the rustle. For a long time, the creature remains elusive, hiding behind the vibrant cover of fresh leaves. Patience, however, yields its reward. A sudden movement draws the eye, and there, perched upon a slender twig, is the tiny architect of the sound: a green linnet.

It is a striking little creature, though effortlessly disguised. Its plumage, a radiant tapestry of olive-greens and soft yellows, mimics the very leaves that shelter it. It flits from branch to branch with restless, joyous energy, a living gem amidst the emerald canopy. One moment it sits in clear view, bathed in a beam of sunlight; the next, with a swift flutter of wings, it dissolves into the shadows of the tree, its form disappearing completely into its environment. 

Then, the bird begins to sing, and the quiet orchard is instantly transformed. The song erupts from its small chest—a cascade of clear, triumphant notes that ripple through the afternoon warmth. It is an astonishingly rich melody, overflowing with an intensity that seems far too grand for so small a singer. Listening to this exuberant hymn, a deep realization washes over me: this solitary warbler is no ordinary bird. It is the true genius loci of the season, the supreme spirit of May incarnate. In its voice rests the collective voice of spring itself—a celebration of warmth, rebirth, and life renewed.

What makes the linnet so captivating is its complete, unselfconscious unity with nature. Nestled within the leafy shadows, disguised by its own feathers, the bird requires no audience, no praise, and no purpose beyond the simple act of being. Its song is not a performance, but a spontaneous overflow of delight. In its masterful camouflage and solitary music, the linnet embodies the ultimate truth of the natural world: an unbridled, self-contained joy that exists purely for its own sake. To witness it is to be reminded that the deepest happiness is often found in quiet places, tucked away among the leaves, singing simply because the sun is shining and the world is alive.

Beneath the apple boughs I rest,
Where quiet noon glides soft and slow;
The earth wears April on her breast,
And all the world is white with snow—
Not winter’s chill, but petals pale,
That drift upon the gentle gale.

A roof of blushing blossom weaves
A bower of mingled light and shade,
Where sunlight flickers through the leaves,
In quiet glades by nature made.
The air is rich with sweet perfume,
A temple carved of bud and bloom.

And lo! Upon a swaying spray,
A tiny, winged spirit alights,
To chase the shadows of the day
Into a thousand sweet delights.
With swelling throat and ecstasy,
He pours his soul in melody.

What hidden joy inspires thy strain,
Thou minstrel of the verdant spring?
Thou know’st no grief, no human pain,
No sorrow that the years must bring.
Thy song is life, untamed and bright,
A cascade of pure, golden light.

Sing on, wild bird! And let me drink
The bliss that overflows thy breast,
Until upon this grassy brink,
My weary spirit finds its rest.
My soul takes wing to soar with thee,
Immortal, radiant, and free.

The verdant canopy of May
Is bright with morning's early gold;
Upon a flowering hawthorn spray,
A little monarch doth unfold
His russet breast and joyful wing,
To rule the kingdom of the glade,
Where every blossom seems to sing,
Within the tender, woven shade.

Across the dew-bespangled lawn;
A gentle sovereign of the plain,
Who bids the shadows of the dawn
Dissolve before his sweet decree,

The listening winds their silence break.

No earthly prince in velvet drest

He greets the season’s golden gate.
The woodland bows beneath his trill,
The brook replies in silver tone,
And over verdant vale and hill,
May wears his music as her throne.

Sing on, sweet herald of the year!
Teach me the secret of thy joy,
Unmoved by mortal grief or fear,
Which worldly troubles ne'er destroy.
For in thy small and feathered frame
Lives Spirit unconfined and free,
That kindles Spring’s eternal flame,
And binds the human heart to thee.

The morning wears a crown of liquid light,
The hazel boughs are soft with newborn green;
Here in the quiet grove, away from sight,
I rest alone, contented and unseen.

Bright beams of amber pierce the leaf-laced shade
To paint the mossy earth in dappled gold,
While through the stillness of the sunken glade
The gentle charms of blooming spring unfold.

Then softly breaks a stir among the boughs—
A tiny songbird, quick with restless glee!
He flits across the shade the hazel houses,
A golden spark that dances wild and free.

From stem to slender twig he lightly bounds,
Shaking the dewdrops from the leafy lace,
And spills a sudden burst of silver sounds
To wake the silence of this sacred place.

He tilts his head to catch the sunny ray,
A playful acrobat of air and wing,
Then leaps into the light and swoops away,
Leaving the sunlit wood a richer thing.

In solitude, my grateful spirit rests;
I ask no more than what is gathered here:
The amber warmth, the hazel’s emerald crest,
And one small bird to make the morning clear.
